learning_objectives.en: Follow a spoken process and label stages without adding information absent from the lecture.
learning_objectives.vi: Theo dõi quá trình qua lời giảng và điền nhãn từng bước, không thêm kiến thức ngoài.

content.en: Look for signposting: first, next, after that, finally, and to summarise. These cues identify order; they do not necessarily introduce an answer immediately.
content.vi: Nghe first, next, after that, finally và to summarise. Chúng chỉ thứ tự; không phải ngay sau từ nối luôn là đáp án.

strategies.en: Identify the starting point and the direction of arrows; predict whether labels are nouns or action verbs.
strategies.vi: Nhìn điểm đầu và hướng mũi tên; đoán nhãn cần danh từ hay động từ.

common_mistakes.wrong: A signpost is always a gap answer.
common_mistakes.correct: It can merely introduce a stage.

reason.en: Sequence cues and content have different functions.
reason.vi: Tín hiệu thứ tự không đồng nghĩa đáp án.

audios.title: Original prototype lecture: how shale gas is extracted
audios.transcript:
Lecturer: Good afternoon. The next example in our energy lecture is shale gas extraction. We are not deciding whether it should be used everywhere. Our purpose is to understand the sequence and evaluate the claims people make about it.
First, a company selects a site and drills a deep well. The drilling equipment passes through different layers of rock. Protective steel casing and cement are then placed inside the well to separate it from underground water.
Next, engineers may turn the well horizontally into a gas-bearing layer of shale. A mixture of water, sand and small quantities of other substances is pumped into the rock under pressure. This creates tiny cracks. The sand helps keep some of these cracks open so that trapped gas can move towards the well.
After that, gas and some of the fluid travel back to the surface. The gas is collected, while the returning water must be stored and managed carefully. Finally, once production ends, the site requires monitoring and restoration.
There are two viewpoints we should distinguish. Supporters argue that shale gas can provide energy while other power systems are developed. Critics point to risks such as water use, methane leaks, and local traffic. The evidence depends on the geology, regulations and the quality of each project. Do not conclude that every site will produce the same benefits or costs.
To summarise, the stages are drilling, sealing, creating small cracks, collecting gas and managing the site. Notice that the phrase to summarise signals the conclusion, not another stage.
